title: Interpretation of Scripture
definition: The Interpretation of Scripture is the faithful process of seeking the meaning God intended in His Word so it may be believed, taught, and obeyed.
summary: The Interpretation of Scripture is the faithful process of seeking the meaning God intended in His Word so it may be believed, taught, and obeyed.
christFocus: Jesus interpreted Scripture as the true witness to Himself, and faithful interpretation helps believers see Christ without forcing meanings God did not give.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Interpreting Scripture means asking what the text truly means, not what we want it to mean. Believers should read carefully, honor context, pay attention to words, compare Scripture with Scripture, and remain humble under God’s authority.

Because Scripture is God’s Word, interpretation is a serious act of discipleship. Misinterpretation can confuse believers, harm the wounded, excuse sin, or place burdens on people God has not placed. Faithful interpretation protects the Church and honors the Lord.

Christ is the center of Scripture, but that does not give us permission to invent meanings. Faithful interpretation sees how the passage truly fits within the Gospel, the character of God, and the redemptive work of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people have heard Scripture used carelessly, sometimes to shame or control them. Faithful interpretation helps rebuild confidence that God’s Word is good, even when human handling of it has been wrong.

This doctrine also corrects the habit of treating the Bible as a collection of inspirational phrases. Scripture must be understood before it is applied.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Handle Scripture with humility and care. Before applying or teaching a passage, ask what it meant, how it fits its context, what it reveals about God and Christ, and how the Holy Spirit calls you to respond.
